solver.kind: blind AI solver B (separate agent, answer-free packet, adversarial rubric)

S059-01.notes: 'Dismissed as' needs a pejorative term for plainness; 'barren' fits. 'Restrained' describes plainness but is approving, not dismissive, and matches her own view rather than the reviewers' contrast. 'Ostentatious' contradicts plainness; 'derivative' is about originality, unsupported.

S059-02.notes: 'Seemed merely ___' plus later reappraisal requires a mildly negative judgment about fussiness over exact terms: 'pedantic'. 'Rigorous' is the later, positive recognition and clashes with 'merely'. 'Careless' contradicts insistence on exactness; 'eloquent' off-topic.

S059-03.notes: Convergence occurred across generations of learners, with no wild-type model present. D is the main trap: it attributes change to individual untutored males over time, but the founders' sons copied abnormal songs; change was generational. A unsupported; C contradicted (sons copied). Factually consistent with Feher et al. 2009 (Nature).

S059-04.notes: Text 2 attributes the small, brief gain to mood/alertness, not Mozart. A overstates (no claim of fabrication); B accepts the 'smarter' framing Text 2 rejects; C unsupported. Facts consistent with Rauscher et al. 1993 and Nantais & Schellenberg 1999 (story vs. Mozart, preference) / Thompson et al. 2001 (arousal-mood).

S059-05.notes: Restrictive 'such as' phrase, no punctuation needed. B opens a nonessential element without closing comma before 'can'; C puts comma between 'such as' and its object; D colon after 'like' does not follow an independent clause.

S059-06.notes: 'Since 1850' with ongoing period to present requires present perfect 'has collected'. 'Had collected' needs a past reference point; simple present/past do not fit 'since'.

S059-07.notes: Doubt about telescope reliability contrasts with confirmation of observations: 'Even so'. 'Therefore' reverses logic; 'For example'/'Similarly' imply support/parallel. Fact check: confirmations in 1610-1611 (Jesuits of the Collegio Romano, Harriot, Kepler) are accurate; Kepler actually used a Galilean-made telescope, but 'other astronomers using their own instruments' is acceptably general.

S059-08.notes: Only B states the shrinkage and its causes (drought and irrigation). A and C give no causes; D gives one cause but never says the lake shrank. The ~90 percent figure since the 1960s is the widely cited figure (some recent studies note partial stabilization, but this is not an error for notes-based item).

S059-09.notes: A states the shared method (inferring an unobserved structure from measurements). B emphasizes difference; C and D each cover only one scientist. Facts on Lehmann (1936 inner core from seismic records) and Tharp (1950s soundings revealing Mid-Atlantic rift valley) are accurate.
